takeaways.text: Revenue from high-bandwidth memory — the chips stacked beside AI processors — passed $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time, and data-center revenue overall tripled from a year ago. AI demand is now the center of Micron's business.
takeaways.title: HBM crossed $1 billion

takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 36.8%, double the 18.5% of a year ago, as prices for both DRAM and NAND kept recovering. In memory chips, price swings matter more than volumes — and prices were Micron's friend this quarter.
takeaways.title: Margins rebuilt

takeaways.text: Revenue dipped from the prior quarter's $8.71B, a pause after a run of records. Management said to expect a new record in the next quarter, with demand growing in both data centers and consumer devices.
takeaways.title: A sequential step down, guided back up

verdict: Micron's revenue rose 38% from a year ago to $8.05B as AI demand filled its data-center order books — HBM revenue passed $1B for the first time — and it kept $1.58B as profit, though sales dipped from the prior quarter's $8.71B.
